cases.findings:
• Pleural disease:
  - Multiple pleural masses are present in the right hemithorax.
  - A dominant posterior pleural mass extends from the posterior RUL apical segment to the RLL posterobasal segment, with an axial long axis of 105 mm on current CT and 98 mm on PET/CT (TL1).
  - A second mass involving the RLL posterobasal-laterobasal segments has an axial long axis of 100 mm on current CT and 80 mm on PET/CT.
  - Atelectatic changes are present in the adjacent lung parenchyma.

• Lungs/airways:
  - No active infiltrative process is identified in the bilateral lung parenchyma. Emphysematous changes are present.
  - The trachea and bilateral main bronchi are patent, without occlusive pathology.

• Mediastinum/esophagus:
  - Soft-tissue-density mediastinal masses are present, with larger lesions posterior to the SVC-RA junction; these are favored to represent multiple metastatic lymphadenopathies in the mediastinum.
  - The thoracic esophagus is normal in caliber, without significant pathologic wall thickening.

• Response assessment:
  - The sum of the 4 target lesions is 264 on current CT and was 225 on prior PET/CT, representing a 17% increase and classification as stable disease.
  - Non-target lesions have also increased in size. No newly developed lesion is identified.

• Included upper abdomen:
  - No free fluid or loculated collection is identified.
  - More conspicuous thickening is present in the right adrenal body and lateral crus.
  - An increased number of celiac-region LNs is present at the level of the portal hilum; short-axis diameters do not exceed 1 cm.

The cardiothoracic ratio is within normal limits, and the major mediastinal vascular structures are normal in caliber. Millimetric mediastinal lymph nodes do not meet pathologic size criteria. No hilar lymph node of pathologic size or configuration is identified.

Circumferential wall thickening of the distal esophagus produces secondary luminal narrowing. One or two millimetric paraesophageal lymph nodes are present.

There are diffuse bilateral pleuroparenchymal sequelae and marked emphysema, including bilateral apical changes, sequelae along the right minor fissure, pleuroparenchymal sequelae in the posterior segment of the right upper lobe adjacent to the fissure, and densities compatible with pleuroparenchymal sequelae in a lower lobe superior segment. Irregular nodular densities are present in the central peribronchovascular region of the apicoposterior segment of the left upper lobe, with similar amorphous peribronchial densities more caudally. Irregular nodular lesions are also present in the right upper lobe, a lower lobe superior segment, and the left lingular segment. A posterobasal pulmonary nodule measures 3 mm. Centriacinar amorphous densities are present at the anterobasal level. Ground-glass opacities and branching centrilobular opacities (tree-in-bud pattern) are present in the superior segment of the left lower lobe. Neither pleural effusion nor pneumothorax is identified on either side.

The liver demonstrates decreased attenuation consistent with hepatosteatosis. The bilateral adrenal glands are normal, without a space-occupying lesion. The surrounding soft-tissue planes are unremarkable. Degenerative osseous changes and increased dorsal kyphosis are present.

- Right lung: Right apical pleuroparenchymal sequelae with traction bronchiectasis. Stable amorphous calcification caudally in the anterior segment of the RUL.
- Right pleural space: New basal pleural effusion measuring 20 mm at its thickest portion. New mild adjacent atelectasis.
- Upper abdomen: Prominent left hepatic and caudate lobes. Perihepatic and perisplenic effusions. Perihepatic effusion remains evident. Splenomegaly. Millimetric gallbladder-neck calculus, not previously clearly identified. Pancreas normal. Bilateral adrenal glands normal. If chronic liver parenchymal disease is clinically considered, I recommend liver evaluation.
- Kidneys and mesentery: Bilaterally reduced renal size. Lobulated bilateral renal contours. CRF remains a consideration. Mesenteric fat stranding.
- Anterior diaphragmatic region: Bilateral LNs. Largest LN on the right measures 21 x 13 mm. Surrounding soft-tissue planes normal.
- Osseous structures: Dorsal kyphosis. Squared vertebral bodies. Thickened, dense paravertebral longitudinal ligaments. I consider these findings suggestive of spondyloarthropathy.

Right cerebral peduncle: Volume loss and increased signal are present. I consider this combination secondary to Wallerian degeneration.

Brainstem/left cerebral hemisphere: No pathologic contrast enhancement.

cases.findings:
First, the trachea and both main bronchi are in the midline, without an obstructive endoluminal lesion. Next, mediastinal assessment is limited (on this noncontrast examination); as far as visualized, the main mediastinal vascular structures and cardiac contour and size are normal. I identify a calcified atheromatous plaque in the proximal left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD). No pericardial effusion or thickening is present. The thoracic esophagus is normal in caliber, without significant tumoral wall thickening, and there are no pathologically enlarged lymph nodes (prevascular, preparatracheal, subcarinal, bilateral hilar, or bilateral axillary).

In both lungs, there is a mosaic attenuation pattern (small airway disease versus small vessel disease). No pulmonary mass or active pneumonic infiltrate is detected. There is no pleural effusion or thickening.

In the included upper abdomen, the liver is diffusely decreased in attenuation (hepatosteatosis). The remaining visualized upper abdominal organs are normal. Both adrenal glands are normal, without a space-occupying lesion. Finally, the thoracic vertebral body heights are preserved, with bridging syndesmophytes along the right anterolateral corners of the thoracic vertebrae (findings consistent with diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis).

Stable left lower paratracheal mediastinal lymphadenopathy measures 32 mm in short axis. Multiple malignant nodules in both lungs are new. Left lingular and right upper-lobe ground-glass opacities and right lower-lobe and mediobasal left lower-lobe consolidation (with diffuse air bronchograms) may reflect infection. The pattern is not typical for COVID-19, but COVID-19 cannot be ruled out; clinical and laboratory correlation is recommended. Overall, findings favor progressive disease.

cases.findings:
Clinical context and comparison: In the setting of an operated craniopharyngioma under follow-up, the sellar and suprasellar abnormality is characterized below. Comparison is made with CT dated [date_1].

Sellar/suprasellar region and ventricular system: A recurrent heterogeneous craniopharyngioma measuring approximately 36x26 mm fills the sellar and suprasellar cisterns and extends into the third ventricle, resulting in narrowing and obstruction of the third ventricle. The mass size is increased compared to the previous examination. The pituitary gland remains separately discernible inferior to the mass. The optic chiasm and both anterior cerebral artery (ACA) A1 segments are displaced anteriorly. Enlargement of the bilateral lateral ventricles and third ventricle is present and was also present on the examination from the early postoperative period.

Ischemic-gliotic and postinterventional changes: Sequela ischemic-gliotic foci involve the bilateral periventricular white matter, corona radiata, and centrum semiovale. A defective appearance of the corpus callosum is attributable to old intervention.

Left maxillary sinus and adjacent structures: A mass fills the left maxillary sinus and extends into the nasal cavity adjacent to the left inferior nasal concha, with an associated defect of the medial wall of the left maxillary sinus. Superiorly, defects involve the upper wall of the left maxillary sinus and the inferior orbital wall, accompanied by minimal intraorbital soft-tissue extension. Additional bone defects involve the lateral wall of the left maxilla and, inferiorly, the pterygoid bone. The mass has malignant features in appearance, invades the hard palate, and demonstrates anterior soft-tissue extension at the left maxillary body. This mass was absent on the [date_2] examination.

Additional observations: Left mastoiditis is present. Apart from the specifically described defects, the remaining cranial osseous structures are normal. Both globes, the retrobulbar fat, and both optic nerves are normal. The optic chiasm is otherwise normal in appearance despite the anterior displacement described above.
